# HELP scylla_manager_scheduler_last_success Start time of the last successful run as a Unix timestamp. The start time is reported, and not the end time, because it describes the state of the data the run worked on - a repair makes the data as fresh as of the moment it started, and a backup stores the snapshot taken at that moment.
# TYPE scylla_manager_scheduler_last_success gauge
scylla_manager_scheduler_last_success{cluster="b703df56-c428-46a7-bfba-cfa6ee91b976",task="965f4f5c-c7d1-4ae6-b770-a2225df4ef49",type="backup"} 1.6456e+09
# HELP scylla_manager_scheduler_task_run_start_seconds Start time of the last task run as a Unix timestamp. Together with "task_state" it tells for how long a task has been running.
# TYPE scylla_manager_scheduler_task_run_start_seconds gauge
scylla_manager_scheduler_task_run_start_seconds{cluster="b703df56-c428-46a7-bfba-cfa6ee91b976",task="965f4f5c-c7d1-4ae6-b770-a2225df4ef49",type="backup"} 1.6456e+09
